description: Somos Astrallis, un equipo conformado por dos chicas apasionadas por la ciencia, la tecnología y la exploración espacial. Nos caracteriza la curiosidad, la creatividad y el deseo de aprender y descubrir cosas nuevas. Combinamos nuestras habilidades en investigación, programación y diseño para desarrollar ideas, resolver problemas y aportar soluciones innovadoras. Creemos en el poder de trabajar juntas y en que las grandes ideas comienzan con la curiosidad de explorar.
summary: TerraTwin is a web application that compares regions of Mars and the Moon with Earth sites documented as possible analogs. Users select a reference region (Jezero, Gale, Gusev or Marius Hills) and obtain a ranking of 10 documented analogs, including Lake Enriquillo and the Baní Dunes in the Dominican Republic, based on five sourced criteria. A Discovery module goes further: it reads slope and relief measured by NASA's MOLA (Mars) and LOLA (Moon) altimeters and searches NASADEM terrain on Earth, at the same scale, for new candidate zones. Every value is labeled as measured, documented or estimated, and missing data is shown as "no data", never as zero. The similarity index is a measure defined by our algorithm, not a probability. TerraTwin helps scientists and mission planners decide where to rehearse planetary exploration on Earth, using transparent and reproducible sources.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

TerraTwin, developed by Team Astrallis, addresses the challenge of identifying Earth locations that analog the permanent Moon base sites and Mars. The application has six sections: Home, Explorer, Map, Analysis, Discovery and Reports.

- Explorer ranks 10 documented Earth analogs against a selected reference region using five criteria: formation type, lithology, minerals, documented water or ice, and geomorphological processes. The similarity index is the number of criteria met out of those that can be compared. Criteria without data are excluded, never counted as zero.

- Map shows where each analog is located on Earth.

- Analysis presents a criterion-by-criterion comparison, measured topography (NASADEM) and estimated climate (NASA POWER) for each analog. Climate also covers sites outside NASADEM coverage.

- Discovery measures the median slope and relief of a 10 x 10 km window of the reference region using MOLA (Mars) or LOLA (Moon), then scans NASADEM tiles on Earth, averaged to the same scale (about 470 m per pixel), and groups matching windows into new candidate zones. Water-covered windows are excluded using the NASADEM water mask. Users can adjust the tolerances.

- Reports generates downloadable files with the parameters used, limitations and sources.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Information about terrestrial analogs is scattered across papers and databases. TerraTwin brings it into one transparent tool that supports the selection of sites for rover testing, crew training and instrument validation. It also places Dominican sites, Lake Enriquillo and the Baní Dunes, within the conversation on planetary analogs, and it is educational for students and the general public.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

Python 3.11, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, rasterio (windowed reading of remote global mosaics), Folium, OpenPyXL, VS Code and GitHub. Data: NASADEM (NASA LP DAAC), MOLA, LOLA and NASA POWER.

CREATIVITY

TerraTwin compares Mars and Moon topography with Earth terrain at the same scale and finds new candidate zones beyond a fixed list. Every value carries its provenance (measured, documented or estimated), and the tool treats missing information as "no data" instead of filling gaps.

FACTORS CONSIDERED BY OUR TEAM

Scientific honesty guided the design. The similarity index is an algorithmic measure, not a probability or proof of a validated analog. The ranking covers 10 documented analogs, not a global search. Part of the validation is circular, because the analogs were chosen for their relationship to Mars and the Moon. Discovery compares only slope and relief, not composition, minerals or water, and with flat reference regions almost any plain matches. Tolerances and thresholds are team parameters, not scientific values. NASADEM does not cover latitudes beyond 60 N and 56 S, so some sites have no topographic data. Climate values are estimates from a coarse reanalysis. Lunar coordinates in our database are approximate.

PLANNED NEXT STEPS (not yet implemented)

Additional lunar regions, elevation sources for polar sites, mineral composition data, validation with domain experts and an open catalog of Dominican analogs.
